content.text:
I identify a single phase: CaTbMn2O6 (mp-1227156).

1. **Single-phase fits:** CaTbMn2O6 was the only candidate that fits well, with R = 0.61 at 0 % strain. It accounts for all the main observed peaks: about 19.8/20.5, 26.1, 32.1/32.9/33.4, 40.9, 51.5, 53–54, 61.6, 67–69 and about 74°. CaPr(BiO3)2 (R = 0.99) and Li3BiO4 (R = 0.995) leave nearly the whole pattern unexplained.
2. **Residual after CaTbMn2O6:** the leftover is mostly paired positive and negative swings at the main peak positions, largest around 33°. That pattern means the peak positions or shapes don't quite match. It isn't an extra set of peaks from another phase.
3. **Two-phase fits:** adding AgAuO2, KAgO2, RbSmO2 or Cs2O2 as a second phase gave weights of 0 to 4 % and lowered R only from 0.6105 to about 0.606. None of them is needed.

Two limits on this. An R of 0.61 is high for a correct phase, which is part of why I've put confidence at 0.8. I did not run fits for KBaTbBiO6 or Ba2LaTaO6. Their larger perovskite cells would put their strongest peak well below the observed 32.9°, so I don't expect either to be present, but that is an estimate, not a tested result.

{"present": ["mp-1227156"], "confidence": 0.8, "note": "CaTbMn2O6 alone explains all major reflections, its residual shows only peak-position/shape mismatch, and no second candidate added meaningful weight or improved the fit."}
